name: Asian Tofu Soba Noodle Bowl with Edamame, Cucumber & Asparagus

instructions.primary_message: Cut the tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich the tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 (1 inch) pieces ginger root
1 ½ small bunches asparagus
1 small bunch green onions (scallions)
1 ½ English cucumbers

instructions.primary_message: Peel and mince or grate the ginger; transfer to a small bowl. Add vinegar, soy sauce, oil, sugar, and sesame seeds; whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ cup rice vinegar
extra virgin olive oil
1 tbsp brown sugar
1 tbsp sesame seeds

instructions.primary_message: Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus. Add to the pot of boiling water and cook until tender, 3-4 minutes. Remove with tongs to a colander and rinse with cold water. Set aside on a plate.

Return water to a boil and add the noodles and edamame; cook according to package directions, about 6 minutes. Once done, drain and rinse thoroughly under cold water. Return to the pot and toss with ¼ cup of the dressing. Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
15 oz soba (buckwheat) noodles
1 ½ cups edamame

instructions.primary_message: Large dice the tofu and gently toss in a large bowl with corn starch.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add tofu and cook until golden brown, 2-3 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, trim green onions; cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Add to the pot with the noodles and toss to combine.
To serve, divide noodles and edamame between bowls; top with asparagus, tofu, and cucumbers. Drizzle with remaining dressing and enjoy!
